---
title: "MIDI Keyboard"
subtitle: "Using GrandOrgue with a MIDI-capable keyboard"
---

This page describes how to set up GrandOrgue with a single MIDI-capable keyboard.

1. Connect the touchscreen monitor to the Raspberry Pi (RPi) using an HDMI cable and a USB cable plugged into a white USB 2.0 port. The monitor needs both cables to handle video, audio, and mouse commands.
2. Connect the Behringer UMC204HD USB audio interface to the RPi using a USB cable plugged into a blue USB 3.0 port.
3. Connect the keyboard **MIDI OUT** to the audio interface **MIDI IN**. This enables the keyboard to control the GrandOrgue software. Since the software won't be controlling the keyboard in any way, there is no need for a second MIDI cable.
4. If using an external keyboard or mouse, connect to it to the RPi using either the white USB 2.0 port (preferred) or the remaining blue USB 3.0 port.
5. Connect the power supplies to the RPi and keyboard.

### To summarize

| Connect... |   | ...to... | ...using |
|:-----------|:-:|:---------|:---------|
Monitor | &rarr; | Raspberry Pi | HDMI
Monitor | &rarr; | Raspberry Pi | USB, white port
Audio interface | &rarr; | Raspberry Pi | USB, blue port
Audio interface | &rarr; | MIDI keyboard | MIDI cable[^1]
Computer keyboard / mouse | &rarr; | Raspberry Pi | USB, white first, then blue
Raspberry Pi | &rarr; | AC power |
MIDI Keyboard | &rarr; | AC power |
Headphones or speakers | &rarr; | audio interface (preferred) | Wired (preferred)
: Using a virtual pipe organ on Raspberry Pi with a MIDI-capable keyboard

[^1]: Be sure to connect **MIDI OUT** from the keyboard or organ to **MIDI IN** on the audio interface.
